original_question: Let A map L2(0,1) into an arbitrary Hilbert space Y, assume A is a Hilbert-Schmidt operator with non-closed range, and let k in L2([0,1] x [0,1]) be the kernel of A* A: L2(0,1) -> L2(0,1). If k has limited smoothness, meaning that k is not infinitely many times continuously differentiable on the whole closed unit square [0,1] x [0,1], under what conditions can the operator equation Ax = y nevertheless be severely ill-posed, in particular exponentially ill-posed?
target_in_paper: Open Question 3 in Section 2, posed as a general question about when limited smoothness of the kernel of A^*A is compatible with severe or exponential ill-posedness, and explicitly introduced in the introduction as the companion to Open Question 2 for the composite Hausdorff moment operator A = B^(H) o J. ([tu-chemnitz.de](https://www.tu-chemnitz.de/mathematik/inverse_probleme/fulltext/GH_2022.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's wording: it has the correct domain L^2(0,1), codomain Y as an arbitrary Hilbert space, the Hilbert-Schmidt and non-closed-range assumptions on A, the use of the kernel k of A^*A:L^2(0,1)->L^2(0,1), the intended meaning of limited smoothness as failure of C-infinity regularity on the whole closed unit square [0,1] x [0,1], and the focus on severe, especially exponential, ill-posedness. ([tu-chemnitz.de](https://www.tu-chemnitz.de/mathematik/inverse_probleme/fulltext/GH_2022.pdf))
missing_details: The official formulation says explicitly that severe and exponential ill-posedness are understood in the sense of Definition 1. In that definition, severe ill-posedness means that polynomial lower bounds C i^{-kappa} <= sigma_i(A) do not persist to arbitrarily large kappa, while exponential ill-posedness is the typical severe case described by an exponential upper bound on sigma_i(A). ([tu-chemnitz.de](https://www.tu-chemnitz.de/mathematik/inverse_probleme/fulltext/GH_2022.pdf))

The paper situates the question as a generalization motivated by the specific composite Hausdorff moment operator A = B^(H) o J from equations (4)-(5), so a fully paper-faithful stand-alone version should keep that motivation in view even though Open Question 3 itself is stated for general Hilbert-Schmidt operators. ([tu-chemnitz.de](https://www.tu-chemnitz.de/mathematik/inverse_probleme/fulltext/GH_2022.pdf))

The nearby context explains why the question is asked: Proposition 1 yields only the wide gap exp(-C i) <= sigma_i(A) <= C'/i^(3/2) for all sufficiently large i, so the actual degree of ill-posedness of the composite Hausdorff moment problem remains unresolved. ([tu-chemnitz.de](https://www.tu-chemnitz.de/mathematik/inverse_probleme/fulltext/GH_2022.pdf))

The nearby regularity result is more specific than your draft: for the concrete kernel k in equation (12), Proposition 2 proves k is continuous on [0,1] x [0,1], but even the first partial derivative with respect to s is not continuous there because it blows up as s -> 1 for 0 <= t < 1. This is the precise kernel-smoothness phenomenon motivating Open Question 3. ([tu-chemnitz.de](https://www.tu-chemnitz.de/mathematik/inverse_probleme/fulltext/GH_2022.pdf))

The question in the paper is explicitly open; it asks for conditions under which such severe or exponential ill-posedness can occur, not for a theorem already proved in the paper. ([tu-chemnitz.de](https://www.tu-chemnitz.de/mathematik/inverse_probleme/fulltext/GH_2022.pdf))
refined_question: Motivated by the composite Hausdorff moment operator A = B^(H) o J, let Y be a Hilbert space and let A:L^2(0,1)->Y be a Hilbert-Schmidt operator with non-closed range. Assume that A^*A:L^2(0,1)->L^2(0,1) is an integral operator of the form [A^*Ax](s)=∫_0^1 k(s,t)x(t)dt with k in L^2([0,1] x [0,1]), and that k has limited smoothness in the sense that k is not infinitely many times continuously differentiable on the whole closed square [0,1] x [0,1]. Under what additional conditions can the equation Ax=y still be severely ill-posed, in the sense that polynomial lower bounds C i^{-kappa} <= sigma_i(A) fail for arbitrarily large kappa, and in particular exponentially ill-posed? ([tu-chemnitz.de](https://www.tu-chemnitz.de/mathematik/inverse_probleme/fulltext/GH_2022.pdf))
justification: This draft targets Open Question 3, not Open Question 2. The introduction says that Open Question 3 is formulated precisely to address the possible occurrence of exponential ill-posedness for integral equations whose kernels have limited smoothness, in the course of analyzing Open Question 2 for the specific Hausdorff moment operator A = B^(H) o J. In Section 2, Proposition 1 gives only the rough bounds exp(-C i) <= sigma_i(A) <= C'/i^(3/2) for sufficiently large i, and Proposition 2 then shows that the concrete kernel k of A^*A is continuous but not infinitely differentiable on [0,1] x [0,1]. Open Question 3 is stated immediately after these facts and is therefore the exact paper formulation your draft is aiming at. ([tu-chemnitz.de](https://www.tu-chemnitz.de/mathematik/inverse_probleme/fulltext/GH_2022.pdf))
